stem: How did the U.S. Supreme Court interpret this article in Gibbons v. Ogden (1824)?

options.text: States may control commerce within their borders that involves foreign countries.
States may be subject to federal regulation in matters of commerce.
States may possess the power to regulate interstate commerce.
States may pass legislation that restricts interstate commerce.
States may regulate commerce within their own borders.

visual_elements: The Congress shall have Power . . . To regulate Commerce with foreign Nations, and among the several States. —U.S. Constitution, Article I, Section 8, Clause 3
